verdict.rationale: Graphite documents first-party natural-language interfaces. Agents take plain-language descriptions, generate changes and open draft PRs. Graphite Chat lets users ask questions about PRs, fix failing checks and make edits from the PR page. These cover code and review tasks, but there is no evidence that the product's own operations (stacking, merge queue, settings, sync) can be driven by natural-language commands. GT MCP only lets external agents create stacked PRs, which is adjacent and not credited here. missing for 10: natural-language control of core product operations (stack management, merge queue, configuration), natural-language commands in the CLI, independent or hands-on corroboration that the NL features work as described.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can operate the product with natural-language commands

citations.quote: Describe what you want built or fixed in plain language, and Agents will pull context from your repository, generate the changes, and open a draft PR ready for your review.
With Graphite Chat, you can ask for context on code changes, get instant feedback, and make edits directly from the chat interface without leaving your review workflow.
Ask Graphite to explain what changed in a pull request, highlight potential issues, or provide context about specific code sections.
Diagnose and resolve failing checks directly from your PR page with full context from your CI results.
